title: Evaluator bootstrapping scripts checklist
body:
Purpose:
This note is a pragmatic, operations-oriented checklist for bootstrapping a new model into the evals harness. Focus is on reproducible local dev + CI gating for regressions: small scripts, loader adapter pattern, scoring templates, artifact packaging, and flakiness detection.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target: medium-sized decoder-only and encoder-decoder models (3B–70B) served via local test containers or hosted staging.
- Not covering heavy distro/quantization details — those belong in serving-runtime docs.
- CI runs should be cheap (sampled prompt sets + smoke scoring) with optional larger nightly/regression runs.

Quickstart checklist (high level):
1) Create minimal model adapter: model_name -> loader class implementing load(), generate(), metadata(). Keep under eval_adapters/.
2) Add promptset bundle: prompts/<model-name>/manifest.json + *.jsonl. Include explicit seed and deterministic flags.
3) Add scoring function: scoring/<model-name>-default.py or use scoring/common_rules.py.
4) Add small smoke test: ci/smoke/<model-name>-smoke.yaml referencing a 10-sample promptset.
5) Add regression baseline: artifacts/<model-name>/baseline.zip (contains outputs + checksums).
6) Wire CI job: add pipeline step to .github/workflows/evals-ci.yaml (fast path) + nightly-regressions cron (full pass).
7) Run local smoke: tools/run_eval_local.sh --model <name> --promptset prompts/<model>/smoke.jsonl
8) Confirm deterministic seed alignment and note non-deterministic ops in manifest.

Loader adapter pattern (recommended minimal API):
class AdapterBase:
    def __init__(self, config):
        # config includes model path/weights, device, quantize flag
        pass
    def load(self):
        # returns a callable inference entrypoint
        raise NotImplementedError
    def generate(self, prompt, max_tokens, temperature, seed):
        # returns (text, meta)
        raise NotImplementedError
    def metadata(self):
        # returns {"model_id":..., "params":..., "limits":...}
        return {}

Notes on loader details:
- Keep dependency list minimal. If model needs heavy deps (triton, custom kernels), add a lightweight test mock (MockAdapter) for CI to validate wiring without full runtime.
- Expose deterministic seeding hook. A common flakiness source is non-seeded CPU ops for tokenizers. Document which tokenizers require special flags.

Prompt set packaging conventions:
- manifest.json fields: name, version, created_by, seed_policy (fixed|random), sample_strategy (first-n|random-n|stratified), notes.
- Each prompt entry: {"id":"p-001","input":"...","metadata":{"topic":"code","difficulty":"medium"}}
- Use short prompt lengths in smoke sets. Reserve longer contexts for nightly/regression.
- Tag prompts that are sensitive to model length/kv cache behavior — those should be excluded from fast CI.

Scoring function templates (examples):
- exact_match_scoring(prompt, output, expected): 0/1 match with normalization (whitespace, punctuation).
- semantic_overlap(prompt, output, expected_embedding): cosine similarity threshold + fallback heuristics.
- cluster_based_failure_detector(outputs_batch): flag if >X% outputs share identical trailing tokens (possible truncation bug).

Sample scoring wrapper (pseudocode):
def score_example(ex):
    out = adapter.generate(ex['input'], max_tokens=ex.get('max', 64), temperature=0.0, seed=ex.get('seed', 42))
    if ex.get('expected'):
        return exact_match_scoring(ex['expected'], out)
    else:
        return llm_likelihood_scoring(ex['input'], out)

CI wiring (fast path vs regression):
- Fast path (PRs): run smoke tests (10–25 examples), verify no categorical regressions against baseline checksums and that latency budget met (p50/p95 under threshold).
- Regression (nightly or manual): run full promptsets (~1k examples) including embedding-based scoring and cross-model comparisons.
- If smoke fails, CI should upload a minimal failing artifact (failing prompts + outputs + adapter logs) to artifacts store and link back to PR.

Baseline artifact format and checksums:
- package: ZIP containing outputs.jsonl (list with id,input,output,token_count,latency_ms), manifest.json, meta.txt (adapter git sha, model hash).
- Checksums: compute sha256 of outputs.jsonl. CI compares new sha256 vs baseline; if mismatch, trigger regression report generation.

Regression report template (auto-generated when baseline mismatch):
- header: model, adapter, commit, baseline sha, candidate sha, date
- summary: pass/fail verdict, delta counts (better/worse for each metric)
- top 10 regressions: id, prompt, baseline_output, candidate_output, metric_delta, human_triage_link
- flaky examples list: examples that flip status across 3 repeated runs

Flakiness detection strategy:
- Repeat each smoke example N=3 times with different seeds, mark as flaky if results differ across runs.
- For flakiness in CI: label as flaky rather than failing. Only hard failures (deterministic mismatch) should block PR.
- Keep a per-prompt flakiness whitelist stored in prompts/<model>/flaky_ids.txt to avoid noise.

Operational scripts (tools/):
- tools/run_eval_local.sh: wraps Python runner with venv activation, collects outputs, prints summary.
- tools/package_baseline.py: zips outputs, computes checksum, uploads to s3://redwood-eval-baselines/<model>/
- tools/compare_baseline.py --candidate candidate_outputs.jsonl --baseline-baseline.zip -> writes regression_report.md
- tools/mock_adapter.py: lightweight mock for CI to validate prompt wiring without heavy model deps.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Tokenizer mismatch: ensure adapter.tokenizer_version in metadata; add tokenizer round-trip tests.
- Non-deterministic sampling in smoke tests: enforce temperature=0 or fix seed; for stochastic checks use similarity-based thresholds.
- Large memory spikes: add a memory watchdog wrapper; fail-fast and record OOM logs to artifact bundle.
- Latency variability in CI runners: use percentile budgets and allow short warmup runs before measuring.

Checklist before merging model onboarding PR:
- [ ] Adapter implements load/generate/metadata and includes minimal unit tests.
- [ ] Smoke promptset + manifest present and referenced by smoke CI job.
- [ ] Baseline package created (or mock baseline for early dev) and path added to manifest.
- [ ] Scoring function added to scoring/ or referenced to shared scoring utilities.
- [ ] CI job added to run smoke and upload artifacts on failure.
- [ ] At least one reviewer from applied-ml + runtime has signed off (include perf/safety reviewers if needed).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How to standardize embedding-based thresholds across tasks? propose a small calibration job that runs on a control set and emits recommended thresholds stored in artifacts/<model>/calibration.json.
- Should we version prompt manifests with semantic versioning? (v1: smoke-only, v2: full-regression). Recommend yes.
- Integrate with console rollouts: map baseline artifact sha -> rollout canary gates. Need coordination with product/console team.

Appendix: Useful commands
- local smoke run: ./tools/run_eval_local.sh --model my-new-bert --promptset prompts/my-new-bert/smoke.jsonl
- package baseline: python tools/package_baseline.py --outputs out.jsonl --model my-new-bert --upload
- compare: python tools/compare_baseline.py --candidate out.jsonl --baseline s3://redwood-eval-baselines/my-new-bert/baseline.zip --out report.md

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally minimal and task-oriented. If we get repeated follow-ups, split into a runner CI cookbook + scoring heuristics doc.
version_notes: initial draft focusing on lightweight CI-first onboarding flow
